headline: A Chinese start-up has shown a prototype light source for extreme ultraviolet chip machines, but it was not switched on and TrendForce says commercial use is three to five years away.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 5: the company's figures cannot be checked, the source was not shown running, and Tom's Hardware judges it no big step toward a Chinese EUV machine.
importance_line: It matters to China's effort to replace ASML, the Dutch maker of the EUV machines China cannot buy, and to chipmakers and governments watching that race, but the claims are the company's own and a full machine needs many more parts.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, citing TrendForce, that the Chinese start-up Langdao Silex displayed a prototype extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source, the part of a chip-printing machine that produces the light, at an industry fair in Shanghai, claiming over 15 watts of output, 90 percent domestic parts and more than 100 hours of continuous running. Tom's Hardware notes that the claims cannot be verified, the source was shown without being switched on, and a light source alone does not make a complete machine, so China has not moved significantly closer to its own EUV scanner.
notes: Full text read. The exact day of the demonstration is not given (this week, at a Shanghai fair).
